title: Keel--Mori categorical quotient for a Deligne--Mumford stack with finite inertia
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $\mathcal X$ be a Deligne--Mumford stack over $S$, with stacks, representable diagonals and 2-fibre products as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Define the inertia stack $I_{\mathcal X}$ by taking, over an $S$-scheme $T$, pairs $(x,\alpha)$ with $x\in\mathcal X(T)$ and $\alpha\in\operatorname{Aut}(x)$; its arrows $(x,\alpha)\to(y,\beta)$ are isomorphisms $a:x\to y$ with $a\alpha=\beta a$. Suppose $I_{\mathcal X}\to\mathcal X$, $(x,\alpha)\mapsto x$, is finite: for every scheme $T\to\mathcal X$ its 2-base change is a scheme finite over $T$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Then there exist an algebraic space $M/S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] and an $S$-morphism $p:\mathcal X\to M$ such that composition with $p$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_S(M,Z)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_S(\mathcal X,Z)$ for every algebraic space $Z/S$. Moreover, $p$ is separated, quasi-compact and a universal homeomorphism. Here separated means that its relative diagonal is proper, with properness tested on scheme charts using [def-weil-proper-morphism]; quasi-compact means that after every scheme base change $T\to M$, inverse images of quasi-compact opens of $T$ have quasi-compact underlying point spaces. Universal homeomorphism means that for every base change $\mathcal Z\to M$ by an algebraic stack the map $|\mathcal X\times_M\mathcal Z|\to|\mathcal Z|$ is a homeomorphism. An algebraic stack here is a stack in groupoids with diagonal representable by algebraic spaces and a smooth surjective scheme atlas; smooth means smooth on scheme charts [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The point space consists of field-valued objects modulo isomorphism and common field extension, with topology detected by a smooth scheme atlas. No finite-type hypothesis on $\mathcal X/S$, and no linear-reductivity hypothesis on its stabilizers, is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0DUT, theorem-keel-mori, restricted to Deligne--Mumford stacks over S; definition-categorical-quotient spells out the initial property. The S-structure on the categorical space is the unique factorization of the structure map to S.

proof.text: The etale atlas of $\mathcal X$ is smooth by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], so [lem-sfb-etale-smooth-atlas-fppf-descent] applies to the given etale stack and makes it an algebraic stack in the fppf convention of the source. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-inertia-local-affine-covers] to obtain a set-indexed covering $g_i:\mathcal X_i\to\mathcal X$ of separated, representable, etale maps preserving all automorphism sheaves; each $\mathcal X_i$ has a finite flat affine cover. The inertia hypothesis is exactly the finite inertia projection assumed in the statement. Keep the family within the size universe in [def-weil-size-convention].

source.place: Tag 0DUT, theorem-keel-mori, opening paragraph; Tag 0DUE and criteria.tex Tag 076V.

proof.text: For every $i$ apply [lem-sfb-finite-flat-affine-stack-invariant-quotient] to the chosen finite flat affine cover. This constructs $f_i:\mathcal X_i\to M_i$, with $M_i$ an affine $S$-scheme, by the equalizer ring of the two maps on functions. It is a uniform categorical morphism for all algebraic-space targets, and is separated, quasi-compact and a universal homeomorphism. In particular we use the all-algebraic-spaces assertion of the lemma, not just categoricality for affine targets.

source.place: Tag 0DUT, opening paragraph, invoking Tags 0DUP and 0DUR.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal X_{ij}=\mathcal X_i\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal X_j$. It is DM by [lem-sfb-dm-etale-atlas-calculus]; its projections are representable etale by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] and separated by [lem-sfb-stack-coarse-properties-etale-locality]. They preserve automorphism sheaves: an automorphism of $(x_i,x_j,\phi)$ is a pair $(a_i,a_j)$ with $\phi g_i(a_i)=g_j(a_j)\phi$ by [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Given $a_i$, the isomorphism of automorphism sheaves for $g_j$ gives exactly one $a_j$ solving that equation. The same argument with $i,j$ interchanged works for the other projection, over every scheme and compatibly with pullback. Thus the hypotheses of the etale comparison lemma hold for both projections.

source.place: Tag 0DUT, second paragraph; base change of separated maps (Tag 050F), etale maps, and stabilizer preservation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-stack-stabilizer-etale-comparison] to $\mathcal X_{ij}\to\mathcal X_i$. It gives a scheme $N_i$ separated etale over $M_i$, with $\mathcal X_{ij}\simeq N_i\times_{M_i}\mathcal X_i$. Etale maps are flat by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus], so the uniform categoricality of $f_i$ in [lem-sfb-finite-flat-affine-stack-invariant-quotient] makes $\mathcal X_{ij}\to N_i$ uniform categorical. Do the same over $j$, obtaining $N_j$. These are categorical moduli spaces of the same stack, so unique factorization gives inverse maps $N_i\rightleftarrows N_j$; their composites are identities because this is true after precomposition from $\mathcal X_{ij}$. Denote the identified scheme by $M_{ij}$ and the map by $f_{ij}$. We have both cartesian squares and separated etale maps $M_{ij}\to M_i,M_j$.

source.place: Tag 0DUT, construction of the overlap diagram from Tag 0DUS and uniform categoricality (Tag 0DUR).

proof.text: For $\mathcal X_{ijk}=\mathcal X_{ij}\times_{\mathcal X_j}\mathcal X_{jk}$ the already obtained squares identify its map to $M_{ij}\times_{M_j}M_{jk}$ with a flat base change of $f_j$, so it is categorical by [lem-sfb-finite-flat-affine-stack-invariant-quotient]. The map to $\mathcal X_{ik}$ forgetting the middle object, followed by $f_{ik}$, therefore descends uniquely to $M_{ij}\times_{M_j}M_{jk}\to M_{ik}$. Likewise the diagonal $\mathcal X_i\to\mathcal X_{ii}$ descends to $M_i\to M_{ii}$, and swapping the factors descends to $M_{ij}\to M_{ji}$. Their source and target identities hold after precomposition with the categorical maps, hence hold by uniqueness. Form the schemes $U=\coprod_i M_i$ and $R=\coprod_{i,j}M_{ij}$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]. These operations define identity, inverse and composition on the pre-relation $R\to U\times_SU$. The maps $s,t$ are etale, as this holds on each disjoint open component by [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus].

source.place: Tag 0DUT, proof of the equivalence-relation claim, construction of c,e,i.

proof.text: Fix an algebraically closed field $K$ over $S$. By [lem-sfb-stack-universal-homeomorphism-geometric-points] applied to $f_i$ and its base changes, $M_i(K)=\pi_0\mathcal X_i(K)$ and $M_{ij}(K)=\pi_0\mathcal X_{ij}(K)$. For the latter, use that $f_{ij}$ is a base change of $f_i$ by step 4 and [lem-sfb-finite-flat-affine-stack-invariant-quotient]. The 2-fibre product formula of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] gives a surjection $\pi_0\mathcal X_{ij}(K)\to\pi_0\mathcal X_i(K)\times_{\pi_0\mathcal X(K)}\pi_0\mathcal X_j(K)$: choose an isomorphism between the two images. It is injective because, after choosing isomorphisms of the endpoints, the discrepancy between the chosen comparison isomorphisms is an automorphism of their image in $\mathcal X(K)$, and the automorphism-sheaf isomorphism for $g_i$ uniquely lifts it and corrects one endpoint isomorphism. Consequently $R(K)\to U(K)^2$ is precisely the kernel equivalence relation of $U(K)\to\pi_0\mathcal X(K)$. Applying [lem-sfb-unramified-geometric-equivalence-relation] with the operations of step 5 makes $R\to U\times_SU$ a monomorphic etale equivalence relation on all test schemes.

source.place: Tag 0DUT, equivalence-relation claim: geometric points and stabilizer correction; Groupoids Tag 0DT7.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient] to the schemes $R,U$ of steps 5--6. Define $M$ as the big-fppf sheafification of $T\mapsto U(T)/R(T)$, rather than the presheaf quotient itself. The cited theorem makes $M$ an algebraic space over $S$, gives a surjective etale map $U\to M$, and identifies $R\simeq U\times_MU$. In particular, its sections over schemes lift to $U$ etale locally. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] the maps $M_i\to U$ identify disjoint open components. Restricting the kernel-pair equality to the components $M_i,M_j$ gives $M_{ij}\simeq M_i\times_M M_j$. Hence the two composites $M_{ij}\to M_i\to M$ and $M_{ij}\to M_j\to M$ agree, supplying the overlap equality used in the next step. The family $\{M_i\to M\}$ is therefore a jointly surjective etale scheme cover.

Construct $p:\mathcal X\to M$ on $x\in\mathcal X(T)$. Put $T_i=T\times_{\mathcal X}\mathcal X_i$; these are algebraic spaces etale over $T$. Their images cover $T$: for a field-valued point of $T$, the covering of $|\mathcal X|$ supplies a lift to some $\mathcal X_i$ after common field extension and an isomorphism to the pullback of $x$. This is an object of the 2-fibre product by [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. The field-extension lifting clause of [lem-sfb-stack-chartwise-smooth-etale-calculus] thus gives joint surjectivity after base change. Refine the $T_i$ by etale scheme atlases using [lem-sfb-dm-etale-atlas-calculus]; compositions are etale by the chartwise calculus. On these refinements use $T_i\to\mathcal X_i\xrightarrow{f_i}M_i\to M$. The two maps agree on overlaps through $M_{ij}\to M$ by steps 4 and 7. Since $M$ is a sheaf by [def-trf-algebraic-space], they glue uniquely to $p(x):T\to M$. Pullback along $T'\to T$ has the same restrictions, so uniqueness proves base-change compatibility. An isomorphism $x\simeq x'$ also gives identical restrictions, hence identical maps. This defines an $S$-morphism of stacks restricting to $f_i$ followed by $M_i\to M$.

source.place: Tag 0DUT, construction of f on objects after equation-fundamental-diagram; the omitted naturality follows by uniqueness of sheaf gluing.

proof.text: The square for $\mathcal X_i\to\mathcal X$ above $M_i\to M$ is cartesian. Indeed, pull the comparison $h_i:\mathcal X_i\to M_i\times_M\mathcal X$ back along $\mathcal X_j\to\mathcal X$. Its source is $\mathcal X_{ij}$, and its target is $M_i\times_M\mathcal X_j\simeq(M_i\times_MM_j)\times_{M_j}\mathcal X_j\simeq M_{ij}\times_{M_j}\mathcal X_j$, which is $\mathcal X_{ij}$ by [lem-sfb-affine-stack-stabilizer-etale-comparison] and [lem-trf-etale-relation-quotient]. The resulting functor is the canonical equivalence from that square. These equivalences imply that $h_i$ is fully faithful: on each scheme test, arrows lift uniquely on the covering refinements from step 8 and glue uniquely because isomorphisms form sheaves. For any object of its target, the local preimages have unique overlap isomorphisms inducing its descent isomorphisms; full faithfulness forces the cocycle, and effective object descent in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] glues them to a preimage. Thus $h_i$ is an equivalence. This establishes the square without a geometric isomorphism criterion.

source.place: Tag 0DUT, cartesianness of equation-fundamental-diagram. Equivalent descent argument using the previously constructed overlap squares, instead of Tag 0DUD.

proof.text: Under the cartesian identifications of step 9, the base change of $p$ by $M_i\to M$ is $f_i$. Each $f_i$ is separated, quasi-compact, and a universal homeomorphism by [lem-sfb-finite-flat-affine-stack-invariant-quotient]. The target-cover criterion [lem-sfb-stack-coarse-properties-etale-locality] therefore gives all three properties for $p$. Its universal-homeomorphism conclusion is tested after arbitrary algebraic-stack base change, exactly as required in the item, not merely on schemes or geometric points.

source.place: Tag 0DUT, paragraph following the cartesian-square claim; Tags 06TZ, 0DTL, 0DTQ.

proof.text: Let $Z/S$ be any algebraic space and $a:\mathcal X\to Z$ an $S$-map. The categoricality of each $f_i$ gives a unique $b_i:M_i\to Z$ with $b_if_i=a g_i$. Over $M_{ij}$, the two restrictions of $b_i,b_j$ have the same composite with $f_{ij}$, namely the restriction of $a$ to $\mathcal X_{ij}$. By its categoricality from the flat-base-change clause of [lem-sfb-finite-flat-affine-stack-invariant-quotient], these restrictions are equal. They therefore glue uniquely over the etale cover $\{M_i\to M\}$ to $b:M\to Z$, since an algebraic space is an etale sheaf [def-trf-algebraic-space]. On the covering refinements of step 8, $bp=a$ by construction, so equality follows from the same sheaf condition.

source.place: Tag 0DUT, final categorical-moduli paragraph, with identity base change; explicit overlap equality in place of details omitted.

proof.text: If $b^\prime:M\to Z$ is another $S$-map with $b^\prime p=a$, its restriction to $M_i$ has composite $a g_i$ with $f_i$, hence equals $b_i$ by [lem-sfb-finite-flat-affine-stack-invariant-quotient]. The sheaf condition of [def-trf-algebraic-space] on $\{M_i\to M\}$ gives $b^\prime=b$. Thus composition with $p$ is the stated bijection. All constructions and gluings were over $S$, and no finite-type, Noetherian, or stabilizer reductivity assumption was used.

source.place: Tag 0DUT, uniqueness in the final categorical-moduli assertion; definition-categorical-quotient, Tag 0DUG.

lean.statement: theorem exists_keelMori_finiteInertia_quotient {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : BasedCategory.{v, w} (Over S)) (hX : IsDeligneMumfordModuliStack X) (hfinite : IsRepresentableFiniteModuliMap (moduliInertiaProjection X)) : ∃ (M : AlgebraicSpace S) (p : BasedFunctor X (discreteModuli M.obj.obj)), (∀ Z : AlgebraicSpace S, Function.Bijective (fun a : M.obj.obj ⟶ Z.obj.obj ↦ p.comp (discreteModuliMap a))) ∧ ModuliSchemeTest @IsProper (moduliRelativeDiagonal p) ∧ IsQuasiCompactModuliMap p ∧ (∀ (Z : BasedCategory.{max u v v', max (u + 1) w w'} (Over S)) (a : BasedFunctor Z (discreteModuli M.obj.obj)), IsAlgebraicModuliStack Z → IsHomeomorph (moduliPointMap (moduliTwoFiberFst a p)))
